name: Gotu Kola Centella asiatica
summary: Gotu Kola (Centella asiatica) (Centella asiatica) carries an editorial Grade B rating, but the studies recorded on this profile do not demonstrate that grade. Recorded activity centres on oxidative stress modulation, neurotransmitter modulation and vascular function support, which describes mechanism rather than demonstrated benefit. Noted cautions include sedatives.
description: Gotu Kola (Centella asiatica) botanical profile with evidence, safety, and practical fit.
safetyNotes: RARE LIVER-INJURY WARNING: Oral Centella asiatica (gotu kola) products have been linked to clinically apparent hepatitis with jaundice, typically after several weeks of use. NIH LiverTox grades this a probable but rare cause (likelihood C); one reported case recurred on re-exposure. The identity and possible contamination of the implicated commercial preparations were not fully established. Stop the suspected product and seek urgent medical assessment for jaundice, dark urine or other signs of liver injury; avoid rechallenge after suspected injury. Use caution with existing liver disease, pregnancy, breastfeeding and sedatives.
contraindications: Past suspected Centella-associated liver injury: avoid rechallenge
Existing liver disease: consult a qualified clinician before oral use
Pregnancy or breastfeeding: avoid because of insufficient safety evidence
interactions: Sedative medicines: potential additive drowsiness; clinical interaction evidence is limited
evidenceLevel: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies
